name: @axs/studio
description: AmberX AI Studio — the SDK subsystem. Depends on @axf/core; core never depends on this.
//deps: Next, React and their types are pinned to the same ranges the GizmoX root
uses, so those particular versions are already familiar even though studio
has its own node_modules by design (a nested Next app sharing GizmoX's
modules cannot be told apart from it) — there is no hoist and no workspace
link for any of them, this package.json is the real install.
@mui/material, @emotion/react and @emotion/styled were ADDED 2026-08-09,
owner-authorised (axf-mui.bmpx), pinned to the same ranges the GizmoX root
uses. This is a genuine local install, not a hoist: it downloaded 78
packages into packages/studio/node_modules that were not there before.
This note used to end 'packages/core stays MUI-free'. That was REVERSED
later the same day by the owner: everything built from here on is MUI, so
the MUI theme became a contract OF the framework and core now owns the
bridge (core/src/theme/mui.ts + MuiBridge.tsx). Core declares the kit as
PEERS; studio's install is still the one that runs, and `npm run link:kit`
(also postinstall) makes core resolve THESE files rather than a second
copy. Two copies is not a tidiness issue — it produced a ThemeProvider
that silently reached nothing. test/mui-singleton.test.ts holds it.
@mui/material-nextjs was added at the same time, for ONE reason:
options.enableCssLayer on AppRouterCacheProvider. MUI 9.3 does not ship
inside @layer mui by default and the layered cache can only come from a
provider. It is NOT here for the SSR style flush — that was measured
first and Emotion already streams its styles into this app unaided.
@mui/icons-material is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, on purpose, permanently.
Every icon in this app already resolves through the branding pack's dual
--axf-brand-*/--gxb-* publication; a Material icon paints a shipped hex no
theme can reach. Do not add it to reach for a convenient icon component —
use the pack.
@axf/core is a workspace dependency: real, resolvable, and honouring core's
`exports` map. A deep import into core's internals fails to resolve at the
bundler, which is the tier-1 half of the boundary.
